APPLICATION FOR PERMISSION TO VISIT TO TIII SICK WARDS. The CLEWS read the following latter which was address- ed to the Warrington Guardians—Gospel Union Homo.— ' Sharp-st., Orford-lane, Warrington, Jan. 15, 1895. " Gentlemen I tile herein, the liberty to ask you a favour having just written to the matron of the parish infirmary and been instructed by her to apply to you. My friend, Miss Dowell, and myself visited a poor girl there a week or two ago, and were inspired with a strong decision to speak to some of ths patients about the Saviour,and so determined to seek permission to pay an occasional or periodical visit to the sick wards for this purpose. Cur work in Warrington is connected with the Gospel Union, which is in its principles strictly un- sectarian and evangelistic. We have been in the habit of visiting in some of the London hospitals before coming here, and often with goc.d results. It is not our way to interfere with anyone's denominational views, or to work in opposition io anyone else who seeks to help thlse poor people, but simply to place before then the way of salvation from sin and its consequencee, through our Lord Jesus Christ, thus hoping to make their lives brighter for time and eternity. Sometimes, we could sing a hymn in a ward, sometimes read a few versos from God's word, and sometimes have little talks by the bedside as God leads us, and always by permission for we do not believe in force work of any kind. If you ap- prove of our coming will you kindly apply to the alsove address, saying what day and hour would be hest. Sometime on Thursdays would be most convenient for us. In the name 'of Jesus Christ, and our Heavenly Fatlwr, who so loved the world that He gave His only begotten on (John I remain, sirs, yours respect- fully, Emily liiilme,"—lt was decided to refer the letter to the House Committee. The hall was nicely deco- rated for the occasion, and when dancing commenced, the mingling of the various uniforms with the bright dresses of the ladies, made the scene an animated one. div.head: GOOD TEMPLARS.
div.p: GOOD TEMPLARS.

The usual weekly sessson of the Hope of Earlestown Lodge of Good Ternplars was held in the Co-operative gall on Monday evening. Bro. Joseph Anderton pre sided, and there was an exceptionally large attendance of members. One candidate was initiated. Bro. Tuthill " Scotland's First" Lodge was present as a visitor. After the ordinary business was transacted, the lodge was thrown open, and a number of friends put in an appearance. A musical programme was gone through, including a pianoforte solo by Bro. Willis, piano duet by Sister F. Holiday and Bro. Willis, recitations by Sisters Stringer, Martin, and Rylance, and song by Bro. W. Wilson, a very enjoyable evening being spent. MISSIONARY MEETIND AT NEWTON. The annual missionary meeting in connection with St. Peter's Church, Newton on behalf of the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign parts, was held in the ['own Hall, Newton, on Saturday evening. The Rev. H. Monk presided, and was supported by the Rev. J. Carson (Wargrave) and Rev. J. Stevenson of Cape Colony. There was a fair attendance. The Chairman read his annual statement of the work carried en in the parish in aid of the society, and compared the amounts realised by collecting boxes, kc., for several years past. He read out the names of the collectors for the year jest closed, together with theamounts handed in, the snm of £l9 Us. 4d. being raised by 39 colleceors. He concluded with an urgent appeal to others to take boxes. The Rey. J. Stevenson afterwards gave a lengthy address on Missionary work carried on in South Africa, his remarks proving instructive and interesting. At the close, a vote of thanks was accorded him on the motion of air. Liptrott seconded by Captain Royer,. A similar compliment was paid the Chairm an on the motion ot the Rev. J. Carson. The annual sermons for the same cause were preached by the Rev. J. Stevenson in St. Peter's Church on Sunday morning and evening, and in the afternoon the rev, gentlemen gave an address at the children's service. GOOD TEmPLART (EBBNEZER The Earlestown Ebenezer Lodge of Good Templars held its weekly Session on Tuesday evening in the Co- operative Hall. Bre. A. Morris, C.T., presided. There was a good attendance of members and visitors, the lodge being favoured with a visit if the Latchford Lodge members echo were received with honours, after which Bro. Ellison, C.T., of the Latchford lodge pre- sided. A capital program rne of solos, recitations, and readings were given by the members and much enjoyed by all, and afterwards refreshments were partaken rof. One candidate was admitted to membership. Votes of thanks were tendered to the visitors, and suitably acknowledged by Bro. Ellison on behalf of the visitors, after which Bro. A. Morris closed the meeting. BIXTOIea NEAPOLITAN CHOIR:.

Mr. Buxton's Diorama and Royal Speciality Company, have since Tuesday evening occupied the Town Hall at Earlestriwn, and appeared before enthusiastic audiences in their unique and delightful entertainment. Since thiir first appearance in Earlestown the Buxton family have established a reputation, their entertainments be- ing at once refined and pleasing. The choruses are exceptionally well sung, and the individual items are without exception, well received. The singing of Miss Hague is much admired, and the efforts of the Buxton family, both in singing and dancing are fully appre- ciated. A pleasing relief to the vocal items is the ven- triloquial sketches of Captain Alexander Fox, whose I manipulation of the crowd of -figures is really clever. An important item in the programme is the dioramic effects, which are aptly and lucidly described by Madame Buxton, who proves an admirable guide to the various places illustrated. Miss Kitty Woodford still remains a favourite, her humourous renderings being enthusiastically applauded. The choir, in addition to the nightly representations until Tuesday evening next, will give two sacred concerts on Sunday in the Mission Hall, as will be seen from an advertisement.

div.head: NOTES BY THE WAY AT EARLESTOWN
div.p: NOTES BY THE WAY AT EARLESTOWN
(BY AN OCCASIONAL (2ONTItIBUTOR).

The entertainers of the general public in this neighbourhood seem to have died a sudden and violent death. Perhaps the Christmas and New Year holidays may in some measure be accountable for this, but it is a fact that since the birth of the New Year, the opportunities for passing an enjoy- able musical evening have been nil. Of course, we have had a dioramic entertainment at the Town Hall, but that was not a local affair, and for some reason or other the people of Earlestown don't seem to take very kindly to these outside ventures. I cannot see why this should be the case, for 1 am perfectly certain, from experience, that we get a better show from strangers, who are professionals than we can ever expect to do from our local talent But somehow or other, we are so very careful of the proprieties, that we are perhaps too anxious that they shall not be shocked by anything ap- proaching levity. Hard times may also have some- thing to do with it, for where there is little money there cannot certainly be any great desire to spend that little on entertainments. However, we want making up, and the sooner the process is in opera- tion the better.

This week however we are doing a little better, as we are visited by Mr. Buxton's Neapolitan Choir. This choir, from the frequency of its visits, is practically becoming an annual institution, and I am much afraid that a season without the Buxton family, would record a blank in the year's round of regular entertainments. They present a first class variety programme, and perhaps the most impor- tant item on the bill of are, is the diorama, illu- strating nightly, visite at home and abroado The singing is good, and from first to last there is no trace of vulgarity. Now this is just what I like, and I venture to think Mr. Buxton will do his hest to warrant the appreciation of his audiences. The choir is giving a couple of sacred concerts in the Mission Hall on Sunday, which, judging by previous perfermances, should be worth a visit.

I don't know whether the change of party in the I District Council has anything to do with it or not, but somehow or other last Monday night. the gas in some parts of the town took upon itself to suddenly have a holiday, and although many of the shop- keepers prayed "Let there be light," they had in many instances to content themselves with the glimmer of a candle. Much inconvenience was caused, and there was a large amount of grumbling before the matter was rectified, when it was found that the water had invaded the pipes, and had to be expelled with the aid of pumps. This is a bad beginning for the new 'Chairman of the Gas Committee, and it would look as if the water had gone roaming round in this way just for spite. He must look to his laurels.
